source_evidence: When you buy a share of common stock, you own equity in the company and will receive any dividends declared and paid by the company. When you buy a corporate bond, you do not own equity in the company.
answer: Corporate bonds and stocks represent different relationships with a company. Buying common stock means owning equity; shareholders may receive dividends if the company declares and pays them. Buying a corporate bond means lending money to the company, not owning part of it. The company is legally committed to pay interest and, in most cases, repay principal when the bond matures. Unlike stockholders, bondholders do not share in the company’s profits through ownership, and in bankruptcy bond investors have priority over shareholders in claims on the company’s assets.
